findings.adjudication: Current project Lecture sources support acid-base variable identification and common case classification but do not contain the complete compensation-formula and mixed-disorder algorithm that B5 historically promises. Do not model-fill it. B5 requires an explicit Current Source admission for the stable algorithm or a deliberate narrowing of the B5 owner claim.

B5 must reuse the repaired B3 context-gated K+/acid-base model rather than reintroducing a universal urine-pH four-grid or a second semantic owner. Stored-RBC hyperkalemia must also inherit the B3 storage-lesion/citrate boundary.

Glomerular hematuria is evidence-defined: dysmorphic/acanthocytic RBCs, RBC casts and compatible glomerular protein/inflammatory evidence support the source. Pyelonephritis and genitourinary TB may cause hematuria but are not glomerular-source diseases merely by name.

Preserve the Study three-test recognition list while separating capability: radionuclide renography is the dedicated quantitative split-function tool; CTU/IVU mainly provide anatomic/excretory and side-to-side information and are not capability-equivalent to renography.

Original PDF resolves formal CKD G staging as the GFR axis: G1 >=90, G2 60-89, G3a 45-59, G3b 30-44, G4 15-29, G5 <15 or dialysis. The source Scr values <177/<442/<707/>=707 umol/L are a merged-cell older phase-adjunct row, not five independent Cr thresholds.

Scr >265 umol/L remains Study Precision only, not a Current universal ACEi/ARB contraindication. Current Core uses indication plus post-start creatinine/eGFR, potassium, blood pressure/volume and reversible-cause assessment; eGFR <30 alone is not an automatic stop rule.

Current Core prioritizes refractory/life-threatening electrolyte or acid-base disturbance, uncontrolled volume overload, uremic organ manifestations and overall clinical state. Historical Cr/BUN numbers remain Study Precision. IHD, CRRT and acute PD are all KRT modalities; the Study claim that severe AKI itself excludes PD is preserved only as historical/source-specific exam language.

Historical <130/80 and <140/90 CKD targets remain 306 Source Precision. They are not promoted to an immutable Current clinical target; B7 keeps the renoprotective blood-pressure mechanism and explicitly separates changing guideline targets from the stable first-pass Core.

Keep >=10^5 CFU/mL as the classic clean-voided ASB/source anchor, with women requiring two consecutive specimens for persistence and men one qualifying specimen. Lower counts can still be clinically meaningful in symptomatic or catheter-associated settings, so 10^5 is not a universal symptomatic-UTI exclusion gate.
Preserve the ASB management mainline: treat pregnancy and before urologic/endoscopic procedures expected to traumatize mucosa; do not create routine treatment debt for common nonbenefit groups.

Aminoglycosides retain nephrotoxicity/ototoxicity risk and are not routine simple-cystitis drugs, but the blanket 'UTI does not use aminoglycosides' rule is removed because selected hospitalized pyelonephritis/systemic-UTI contexts may use them intravenously with appropriate monitoring.

WBC casts are high-value support for renal parenchymal/tubulointerstitial involvement, not a required finding in every pyelonephritis case. Location is judged from systemic symptoms, flank/CVA findings, urinalysis/culture and complication context together.

Male=complicated, 3d/7d/2w/6w/6mo regimens, chronic >6 months and IVU 'gold standard' remain explicit 306 Source Precision. Current mechanism Core is structural/flow/host risk, infection location, persistence/recurrence and chronic tubulointerstitial scarring; changing modern classification or treatment guidance is not encoded as timeless physiology.
